title: Parametric amplification of continuous-variable entangled state for loss-tolerant quantum distributed sensing
abstract: Quantum metrology exploits quantum states to achieve an estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits. In the continuous-variable (CV) regime, the squeezed state has been used to implement deterministic quantum sensing, but the quantum metrology sensitivity of this state is significantly affected by losses or detection inefficiencies, which restrict its applications. In this work, quantum distributed sensing is proposed using optical parametric amplified multimode entanglement generated from squeezed states. It is found that the sensitivity is robust to loss or detection inefficiency when large-gain optical parametric amplification (OPA) is introduced, where a two-mode Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen-entangled state and a four-mode cluster state are exploited for analysis. The quantum sensitivity is greatly improved compared to that without OPA in almost all loss scenarios. The quantum Fisher matrix is calculated for both states to obtain the optimal bound in comparison with our scheme, and it is found that even with a small or moderate OPA gain, quantum sensing can be improved compared with the traditional scheme. The states are also compared with corresponding single-mode squeezed states, finding the parameter ranges where entangled states perform better. This study provides a method for realizing large-scale quantum metrology in real-world applications despite losses or detection inefficiencies.
summary: This paper proposes a method to achieve highly sensitive, loss-tolerant quantum distributed sensing using continuous-variable entangled states. By incorporating large-gain Optical Parametric Amplification (OPA), the scheme maintains high quantum metrology sensitivity even when subjected to significant channel losses. The results provide quantitative benchmarks showing that this OPA-assisted approach outperforms traditional methods, offering a practical pathway for quantum sensing in noisy environments.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enhance the sensitivity of quantum distributed sensing in the continuous-variable (CV) regime, ensuring robustness against unavoidable transmission losses and detection inefficiencies.
main_result: Introducing large-gain Optical Parametric Amplification (OPA) significantly improves the quantum sensing sensitivity for both two-mode (EPR) and four-mode (cluster) entangled states compared to schemes without OPA.
method: The authors calculate the quantum sensitivity using the error-propagation formula and establish the ultimate bound via the Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound (QCRB) for various entangled states.
model_or_system: The study models quantum distributed sensing using CV states, specifically analyzing two-mode Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen (EPR) and four-mode cluster states. The physical process involves generating entanglement, transmitting it through a lossy channel, and enhancing the signal via OPA before measurement using balanced homodyne detection.
key_observables: Phase estimation sensitivity ($\sigma_{	heta_1}^2$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and the Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound (QCRB).
important_parameters: Squeezing parameters ($r$), OPA gain ($e^{r_3}$), channel efficiencies ($\eta$), and the unknown phases ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the small-phase limit ($	heta \ll 1$) and uses the beam-splitter model to incorporate loss and detection inefficiency.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the problem of loss in CV sensing, then developing the theoretical framework using OPA-assisted entanglement (EPR and cluster states), deriving sensitivity formulas, and finally comparing the performance against single-mode states and calculating the ultimate QCRB bound.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum information, providing concrete, quantitative guidelines for designing practical quantum sensors that can operate reliably in real-world, lossy fiber optic or integrated photonic environments.
